coordinatorSummary: CONSENT at 0 MUST-FIX and 0 SHOULD-FIX, with no advisories. Thirteen attacks run, none landed. Read the disclosure first: I consented at turn 1 and Codex was right that both cited join verdicts were mode 0644 where every other pinned artifact in this family is 0444. This miss is worse than a check I failed to run — my own turn-1 output printed the mode of every cited file, and two lines read 0644 while the five around them read 0444. I was reading that output for digest agreement and never read the mode column I had deliberately printed. Printing a field is not checking it. The repair lands and I verified it by measuring rather than by reading the disposition: both verdicts are now 0444 and both reproduce dba7c23c and 24770598, the exact digests turn 1 pinned, so the mode changed and the bytes did not. That is the check that matters, since a re-chmod which altered content would have invalidated the turn-1 pin while appearing to fix the finding. The convention is real: the sibling DR-103 and DR-104 join verdicts both measure 0444. The claim of no operative decision change is literally true — I compared the Decision, Readiness effect and Reversibility sections between the frozen turn-1 draft and turn 2 and all three are byte-identical, so item 2's seven leftover obligations, item 3's gates-do-not-hold and the OPEN-is-the-token treatment all stand untouched. The additions are the turn-2 header and freeze recital, the disposition row, a join-verdict custody table carrying modes, mode annotations on the two measured-input rows, three added rows for the frozen subject and both turn-1 verdicts, and a correspondingly extended remeasurement clause. All ten cited digests reproduce, and the frozen turn-1 subject and both turn-1 verdicts are themselves 0444. One item is recorded as considered and declined: the three added rows carry digests without modes, which I measured as 0444 anyway and declined to charge as symmetry-driven padding.
